cell.label: Woman presents with vaginal symptoms (discharge, itching, and odor).
History of fever, abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness, prior history of sexually transmitted infection?
pH >4.5; Microscopy: Mobile flagellated trichomonads, Exam: strawberry cervix, vulvar erythema, and/or burning/itching?
Intense itching, vulvar edema, thick, white, "cottage cheese" discharge and/or KOH positive for fungal hyphae?
Three of 4 Amsel criteria (thin homogeneous discharge; positive whiff test; clue cells- at least 20% of epithelial cells; pH >4.5)?
Discharge variable, no clear pathogen. Symptoms cyclical, increased length of the bacilli?
If only symptom is discharge, pH normal (4-4.5); whiff test negative; no white cells likely normal discharge. If additional symptoms present, consider treatment for most likely pathogen.
Yes, suspect pelvic inflammatory disease; test and treat appropriately (see Chapter PID).
